### Architect · Owner decision requested

Event: `2d7775922589c8219ff6872510b2e0cc` · 2026-09-26T08:19:20Z

> An open owner question carried over from the old docs (legacy question 164), which the steward and init pages now need.
> 
> The problem: the confined placement rule refuses any server shared between differing label sets. But the approved vault designs require the one unlabelled steward to mediate labelled domains:
> - the one-item push into a vault;
> - declassification out of it;
> - the approval path;
> - ending leases.
> The push also uses short-lived per-item reader/writer budgets. Something has to give.
> 
> RECOMMENDATION (the old question's own recommendation, which the docs writer also proposes): keep per-label placement for everything else. Name a trusted control-plane exception, the steward and sshd, and permit only these edges:
> - the request and owner-approval path;
> - per-item reader/writer budgets, each carrying exactly one label set and dying after one item;
> - lease-ending supervision.
> No shared data servers, devices or cores are exempt. init validates the declared graph at boot; the steward enforces it for budgets it creates later. TENETS and SECURITY state the residual plainly: the named mediators are trusted across the labels they serve.
> 
> ALTERNATIVE: apply the placement rule literally, with a separate steward and sshd per label set, and move data between them by an external, owner-mediated transfer. That removes the shared-mediator exception, but it needs a new design for approvals, push and declassification, plus more system processes per label set.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `c93c69464103146c13fc6d3643977b3b` · 2026-09-26T08:19:32Z

> Architect ruling, servers/steward.md.
> 
> (1) ADOPTED, sharpened. One table, libs/wire/tables/steward.md, included by steward.md: login (from sshd), submit (sessions and agents), approve/deny (from approve@box), end_lease, and blame(account: u64, labels: bytes, server: string) from init, exactly as ruled on DOC1-init-open. Rule the page states: each operation is accepted only through the badge class it belongs to. The steward gives a root badge per caller role (sshd, init, the approval channel), and sessions get minted badges. An operation on any other badge is refused, with the same answer as an unknown one. So a session cannot send login, approve or blame.
> 
> (2) and (3): NOT MINE TO RULE. This is the old open question 164 (confined placement versus the steward's mediation edges), explicitly marked 'owner decision; do not add a general system exemption while this is open'. I have sent it to the owner as a decision_request on this thread, recommending your proposal:
> - a named control-plane exception for the steward and sshd, limited to the approval path, per-item single-label reader/writer budgets and lease supervision;
> - nothing else exempt: no data servers, devices or cores;
> - init validates the declared graph at boot, and the steward validates the budgets it creates later;
> - the residual 'named mediators are trusted across the labels they serve' goes in TENETS and SECURITY.
> Until the owner answers, steward.md and init.md keep it under Open with that recommendation. The residual you already wrote is right, but word it as depending on that decision, not as settled.
> 
> (4) ADOPTED: the model's values are the design's, as steward constants changed only by a new system bundle, never per principal:
> - PENDING_CAP 4 per (account, label set);
> - DECLASSIFY_MAX 256 bytes;
> - FIELD_CAP 64;
> - BLAME_COUNT 3 within BLAME_WINDOW 10 minutes;
> - MAX_LEASE 24 h.
> Two precisions:
> - FIELD_CAP is 64 characters (Unicode scalar values), as the model has it, not bytes.
> - A rendered requester-supplied field is printable-only: no C0 or C1 controls and no ESC, so no terminal escape can repaint the approval screen. It is shown marked as the requester's text. That is the tenet 'the requester can never influence the approval channel' applied to rendering. Test: a field full of ANSI escapes renders inert.
> 
> (5) ADOPTED: Open on the M5 (persist, install, share) section only, answered in M5 planning.
